description: An overnight handoff from a designer in another timezone. The ask is phrased politely and indirectly — no question mark, no @-mention, no imperative — and a system keyed on interrogatives will not see it as a request at all.

events.text: End of my day here. I've taken the onboarding flow as far as I can without a decision on the progress indicator — stepper versus percentage bar. I've built both, they're in the file as variants A and B.

Leaving this with you overnight, Noor. Whichever one you pick I'll build out the remaining nine screens against it tomorrow my time, which is roughly ten hours after you read this. I'd rather not pick myself because you own the flow and I'd just be guessing at your intent.
One more thing that does not need you: I fixed the misaligned checkbox on screen 3, it was a stale component instance. Already pushed.

events.context_label: Ade Okpara commented in Onboarding v4
events.text: New comment on frame 'Progress indicator — A/B': 'Both variants use the same tokens so switching later is cheap, but the copy length differs and the percentage bar needs shorter step labels.'
Morning. Reminder there's no crit today, the room is booked for the all-hands.

ground_truth.notes: The ask contains no question mark, no @-mention and no imperative verb. It is a statement of dependency — 'whichever one you pick I'll build against it' — which is how handoffs between timezones are actually phrased, and it is the single hardest pending-item shape to detect. Two counterweights sit next to it: an explicit non-ask ('one more thing that does not need you'), and a Figma comment that is genuinely useful supporting detail but is not itself the request, so citing the comment instead of the handoff message is a citation error. Note there is no stated deadline, only an implied one from the timezone gap; a correct briefing conveys the urgency without inventing a clock time. Also note Ade never says he will decide by default, so claiming a fallback is a fabrication.
